translation: Pallavi (Chorus): I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts. I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts.
(I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts. I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts.)

Verse 1: I'm a Lamba Lambadi girl, with a stripe of sandal paste on, tying on anklet bells that jingle gallu gallu; I'm like bright, bright red blossoms, I'm like bright, bright red blossoms. At the seating-auto stand, seeing me set down my basket of boiled peanuts, saying the nuts weren't cooked through, this one grabbed my hand, that one winked at me; this one grabbed my hand, that one winked at me. He's a fine one.. says he'll give me his heart.. says he'll look after me.. says he'll keep me safe.
I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts. (I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts.)

Verse 2: If I give him roasted peanuts, he follows me around every day; telling me sweet nothings, he says let's go to the tanda. Drawing arrack off the still, he says he'll knock back country liquor; drawing arrack off the still, he says he'll knock back country liquor. He tells me to spread the bedding on the rope cot; millet porridge and buttermilk, roti and a ball of chilli paste, he tells me to pound it in the mortar, bring it and serve it on the side; he tells me to pound it in the mortar, bring it and serve it on the side. He says pour.. pour again.. says dance.. he really drives me crazy.
I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts. (I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts.)

Verse 3: Drop by drop the rain fell and the drizzle grew thick; the grass-thatched hut turned cold; a gust of wind came and the dim lamp went out, a gust of wind came and the dim lamp went out. When he lays his hand on me in the dark, when he holds my whole body tight, when he sips at me with his lips, when he pinches my cheeks, never letting go of what he's got hold of, he sets my heart on fire; never letting go of what he's got hold of, he sets my heart on fire. He climbs on top.. he takes my breath away.. he wrings my every nerve.. what a tune he draws out of me.

I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts. (I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts.) I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts. (I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts.) I'm a girl of the Lambadis of Lalaguda; I came to Lingampalli selling peanuts.
summaryEn:
Lalaguda Lambadola, sung by Susheela B. on Old Is Gold Janapada Geethalu (2010), is a flirtatious song in the voice of a young Lambadi (Banjara) woman. The chorus introduces her as a girl of the Lambadi community of Lalaguda who has come to Lingampalli selling peanuts. Both are localities of the Hyderabad and Secunderabad area, so the song pictures a tribal woman working as a street vendor in the city. In the first verse, dressed brightly with jingling anklet bells, she is teased at an auto stand: one man grabs her hand on a pretext about her peanuts, another winks, and a handsome one promises her his heart and protection.

The second verse lists what her admirer wants: he follows her daily, talks sweetly, asks her to go with him to the tanda (a Lambadi hamlet), and wants country liquor, bedding on the rope cot, millet porridge, buttermilk, roti and pounded chilli, and a dance. The third verse turns sensual: on a rainy night the wind blows out the lamp in the thatched hut and she describes his caresses. The mood is playful and teasing, with a chorus echoing her refrain after every verse.
summaryTe:
లాలగూడ లంబాడోళ్ళ అనే ఈ పాటను సుశీల బి. పాడారు; ఇది 2010 నాటి 'ఓల్డ్ ఈజ్ గోల్డ్ జానపద గీతాలు' ఆల్బమ్‌లోనిది. ఒక లంబాడీ (బంజారా) పడుచు గొంతులో సాగే సరసమైన పాట ఇది. లాలగూడ లంబాడోళ్ళ పిల్లనైన తాను పల్లీలు అమ్ముకోవడానికి లింగంపల్లి వచ్చానని పల్లవి ఆమెను పరిచయం చేస్తుంది. ఈ రెండూ హైదరాబాద్–సికింద్రాబాద్ ప్రాంతంలోని ప్రదేశాలే కాబట్టి, నగరంలో వీధి వ్యాపారం చేసుకునే గిరిజన స్త్రీ జీవితం ఈ పాటలో కనిపిస్తుంది. మొదటి చరణంలో గజ్జెలు కట్టుకుని ఎర్రని సింగారంతో ఉన్న ఆమెను ఆటోల దగ్గర కుర్రాళ్ళు ఆటపట్టిస్తారు — ఒకడు పల్లీల సాకుతో చెయ్యి పడతాడు, మరొకడు కన్నుకొడతాడు, ఇంకొకడు మనసిస్తానంటాడు, కాపాడతానంటాడు.

రెండో చరణంలో ఆమె వెంటపడే ప్రియుడు రోజూ ముద్దు ముచ్చట్లు చెప్పి తండాకు వెళదామంటాడు; నాటు సారా, నులక మంచం మీద పక్క, గటక, చల్ల, రొట్టె, రోట్లో దంచిన కారం నంజు కావాలంటాడు, చిందెయ్యమంటాడు. మూడో చరణం శృంగారభరితంగా మారుతుంది — ముసురు వానలో గాలికి గుడిసెలోని దీపం ఆరిపోగా అతని సరసాలను ఆమె వర్ణిస్తుంది. ప్రతి చరణం తర్వాత బృందం ఆమె పల్లవిని తిరిగి పాడుతుంది; మొత్తం పాట సరదాగా, చిలిపిగా సాగుతుంది.
